column3: An exact collective confession of faith followed by a plea for forgiveness and protection.

It repeats the plea for forgiveness and mercy and the declaration that God is best of the merciful.
A community answers the call to faith with the same Lord-address and a request for forgiveness.
This nearby description identifies believers by reverent fear of their Lord, a disposition behind the focus prayer.
The closing divine attributes of forgiveness and mercy occur in a remote legal setting.
Moses makes a shared plea for forgiveness and mercy, closely paralleling the focus prayer's communal form.
It joins repentance and reform with divine acceptance, forgiveness, and mercy.

It directly defines all creatures as coming to the Merciful as servants, grounding the focus designation.
Jonah's prior glorification offers only a remote devotional parallel.

Angels seek forgiveness for those on earth while God is named Forgiving and Merciful.

It pairs wrongdoing replaced by good with God's forgiveness and mercy.

God turns in mercy toward believers whose hearts nearly swerved in hardship.

God calls the righteous inheritors of the earth "My servants," strengthening the servanthood theme.

Divine provision of food and safety has only a general relation to merciful care.

Those who reject false worship and return to God receive good news as His servants.

A believing group addresses its Lord together under persecution, a related communal prayer setting.

It calls people to seek God's forgiveness so that they may receive mercy.

A group addresses its Lord together for mercy and right guidance in a close prayer parallel.

It condemns treating God's servants as part of Him, clarifying the proper Creator-servant distinction in the focus.

Mercy spread after despair is a general image rather than a link to the collective petition.

Believers who commit a wrong remember God and seek forgiveness rather than persist in it.
Those who wrong themselves seek God's forgiveness and receive prophetic intercession, finding God accepting and merciful.
It directly promises forgiveness and mercy to one who does wrong and then seeks God's forgiveness.

Adam and his wife address their Lord together, confess wrong, and ask for both forgiveness and mercy.

The angels address their Lord on behalf of believers, asking entry into Paradise, protection, and mercy for their families.
The jinn call their people to respond in faith so that God may forgive their sins and protect them from painful punishment.
Believers pray, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith," directly joining communal faith and forgiveness.
Abraham and his companions make a collective Lord-address of reliance, repentance, and return to God.
Believing men and women pray together for their light to be completed and for forgiveness on the final Day.
Noah asks his Lord to forgive himself, his household, and every believing man and woman who enters his home.

Believers ask their Lord not to let their hearts deviate after guidance and to grant them mercy.

Moses's believing community asks God to save them by mercy from the disbelieving people.
